**(p-٦٢٦٨)** In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Surat Quraysh**

Meccan, and its verses are four.

**(p-٦٢٦٩)** In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The discussion on the ta'wil (interpretation) of His saying, exalted is He:

[1–4] ﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh,﴾ ﴿their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer.﴾ ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House,﴾ ﴿Who has fed them against hunger and secured them against fear.﴾

﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh,﴾ ﴿their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer.﴾ Ibn Hisham said: *Ilaf Quraysh* means their being accustomed to going out to al-Sham (Syria) in their trade. They had two journeys: a journey in winter and a journey in summer. He said: Abu Zayd al-Ansari informed me that the Arabs say *aliftu al-shay'a ilfan* and *allaftuhu iilafan*, with the same meaning, and he recited to me the verse of Dhu al-Rummah:

*"From the sand-treading ones, a dark-brown, pure-coloured (mare), the rays of the morning sun showing clearly in her colour."*

*Al-iilaf* also means that a person has a herd (*alf*) of camels, or cattle, or sheep, or something else. It is said: *alfa fulan iilafan*. Al-Kumayt ibn Zayd said:

*"In a year whose people who own herds call it: 'This barren year has left us with nothing but the bare-ribbed (cattle).'"*

**(p-٦٢٧٠)** *Al-mu'im* is the year in which milk has become scarce. *Al-iilaf* also means that a people become a herd (*alf*); it is said: *alafa al-qawmu iilafan*. Al-Kumayt said:

*"And the family of Muzayqiya, on the morning they met the Banu Sa'd ibn Dabba, were a gathered (herd)."*

*Al-iilaf* also means that one makes a thing familiar to someone, so he becomes accustomed to it and keeps to it; it is said: *allaftuhu iyyahu iilafan*. *Al-iilaf* also means that one makes what is less than a thousand (*alf*) into a thousand; it is said: *allaftuhu iilafan*. End of quotation. Because *iilaf* comes with these meanings, the secret of replacing the unrestricted form with the restricted form after it becomes clear, along with what it contains of vagueness, then the explanation contains magnification and affirmation.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ikrimah, who said: The Quraysh had become accustomed to Busra and Yemen, travelling to this one in winter and to that one in summer. And from Ibn Zayd, who said: They had two journeys: in summer to al-Sham and in winter to Yemen, for trade. When winter came, al-Sham was closed to them because of the cold. Their journey in winter was to Yemen.

And from Ibn Abbas, who said: They spent winter in Mecca and summer in al-Ta'if. Most scholars hold the first view. The lam in the saying *li-iilaf* is connected to His saying: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House﴾ (Quraysh 3), meaning: so let them worship Him for the sake of their accustomed security in the two journeys. The fa' (so) has come in because of the sense of condition in the sentence, since the meaning is: the blessings of Allah, exalted is He, upon them are not limited; so if they do not worship Him for all His blessings, then let them worship Him for this great blessing. *Al-Bayt* is the honoured Ka'bah. ﴿Who has fed them against hunger﴾, that is, against severe hunger in which they were before the two journeys. So *min* ("against") is causal, meaning He bestowed favour upon them and fed them to remove hunger from them; or it is substitutive. ﴿And secured them against fear﴾ (Quraysh 4), that is, from what those who were not of the people of the sanctuary feared, such as raids, wars, fighting, and the matters for which the Arabs feared one another; so they were secured from that because of the sanctity of the Haram. He recited: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which the fruits of everything are brought?﴾ (al-Qasas 57). A similar example is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a secure sanctuary while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾ (al-Ankabut 67).

**(p-٦٢٧١)** *Tanbih* (a note):

Some people claimed that the lam in *li-iilaf* is connected to what comes before it, that is: ﴿So He made them like eaten straw﴾ (al-Fil 5) ﴿for the accustomed security of Quraysh.﴾ Al-Shihab said: On this view, it must be interpreted, and the meaning is: He destroyed them and did not give power over the people of His sanctuary, so that they would remain as they were; or He destroyed those who intended them, so that people would take warning and no one would dare to attack them, and thus security would be complete for them in residence and travel. Or it is the lam of consequence (*lam al-'aqibah*). End of quotation.

There is no hiding the artificiality in this; therefore Ibn Jarir said in refuting it: As for the view of the one whose statement we have quoted, that it is connected to His saying ﴿So He made them like eaten straw﴾ (al-Fil 5), if that were so, then *li-iilaf* would have to be part of *alam tara* (Did you not see), and it would not be a separate surah from *alam tara*. The consensus (*ijma'*) of all Muslims that they are two complete surahs, each separate from the other, shows the corruption of the view of whoever said that. And if His saying ﴿for the accustomed security of Quraysh﴾ were part of His saying ﴿So He made them like eaten straw﴾, then *alam tara* would not be complete until it was joined to His saying "for the accustomed security of Quraysh," because the sentence is not complete except with the completion of the report that was mentioned. End of quotation.
